paragraphs.en: If you ever get the {impression} that your dog is so {clever} that it can“ {tell} ”whether you look {content} or {annoyed} , you may be onto something.They {bark} when they sense your {anger} or wag (（摇动）) their {tails} when they see your smile.Dogs may indeed be able to distinguish between happy and {angry} human faces, according to a new study.In this study, researchers {claimed} that dogs can distinguish between human facial expressions, just as a {son} learns to understand his father's emotions.
paragraphs.cn: 如果你曾有过这样的 <u> 感想 </u> ，即你的狗非常 <u> 聪明 </u> ，能够“ <u> 分辨 </u> ”你的表情是 <u> 满意 </u> 还是 <u> 恼怒 </u> ，那你可能有了些发现。它们会在感觉到你的 <u> 怒火 </u> 时 <u> 吠叫 </u> ，或在看到你微笑时摇动 <u> 尾巴 </u> 。根据一项新的研究，狗也许确实能分辨出人类高兴和 <u> 生气 </u> 的表情。在这项研究中，研究人员 <u> 称 </u> ，狗可以分辨人类的面部表情，就如同一个 <u> 儿子 </u> 学会理解他父亲的情绪一样。

paragraphs.en: Researchers trained a group of 11 dogs in a {laboratory} to distinguish between {images} of the same person making either a happy or an angry face.During the training {phase} , each dog was shown only the {upper} half or the {lower} half of the person's face. {Afterward} , the researchers tested the dogs' ability to distinguish between human {facial} {expressions} by showing them the other half of the person's face in images totally different from the ones used in training.The dogs were able to pick the annoyed or {pleasant} face by {pressing} their noses against the image to indicate their choice, performing better than random chance would predict.
paragraphs.cn: 研究人员在 <u> 实验室 </u> 里训练了11只狗，让它们分辨同一个人高兴或生气时的面部 <u> 图片 </u> 。在训练 <u> 阶段 </u> ，每只狗只能看到人脸的 <u> 上 </u> 半部分或 <u> 下 </u> 半部分。 <u> 之后 </u> ，研究人员向狗展示了与训练时完全不同的图片中人脸的另一半，以此测试狗分辨人类 <u> 面部表情 </u> 的能力。这些狗能够通过将鼻子 <u> 贴 </u> 在图片上来表明自己的选择，从而挑选出恼怒或 <u> 愉快的 </u> 表情，它们的表现比随机概率所预测的更好。

paragraphs.en: The study provided {insights} into how dogs apply what they learned about human faces during training to new faces in the {testing} stage.“We can {rule} out that the dogs simply distinguish between the pictures based on a simple {cue} , such as the sight of {teeth} ,”said study {author} Corsin Müller.“Instead, our results suggest that the successful dogs realized that a smiling {mouth} means the same thing as smiling eyes, and the same rule applies to an angry mouth having the same meaning as angry eyes.”
paragraphs.cn: 这项研究让我们 <u> 了解 </u> 到，狗是如何将训练中学到的关于人类面孔的知识应用于在 <u> 测试 </u> 阶段中出现的新面孔的。研究报告的 <u> 作者 </u> 科辛·穆勒说：“我们可以 <u> 排除 </u> 狗仅仅是根据简单的 <u> 线索 </u> （如看到 <u> 牙齿 </u> ）来区分图片的可能性。相反，我们的结果表明，成功完成测试的狗意识到，微笑的 <u> 嘴 </u> 与微笑的眼睛所传达的含义是一样的，同样的规则也适用于愤怒的嘴与愤怒的眼睛，它们传达的含义也是相同的。”

paragraphs.en: “With our study, we think we can now {confidently} conclude that at least some dogs can distinguish human facial expressions,”Müller told Live Science .
paragraphs.cn: 穆勒告诉《生活科学》杂志：“通过我们的研究，我们认为现在可以 <u> 自信地 </u> 得出结论：至少有一些狗是可以分辨人类面部表情的。”

paragraphs.en: At this point, it is not clear why dogs seem to have the ability to recognize different facial expressions.“To us, the most {reliable} explanation appears to be that the basis {lies} in their {living} with humans, which gives them a lot of {exposure} to human facial expressions.”Muller said.It might be a result of careful {adaptation} over thousands of years and it may be one of the reasons why they play a role in the {army} and work with {policemen} .
paragraphs.cn: 目前，我们还不清楚为什么狗似乎拥有识别不同面部表情的能力。穆勒说：“对我们来说，最 <u> 可靠的 </u> 解释似乎是：这种能力的根源 <u> 在于 </u> 它们与人类共同 <u> 生活 </u> ，这使它们有大量机会 <u> 接触 </u> 到人类的面部表情。”这可能是数千年来谨慎地 <u> 适应 </u> 的结果，而这份能力也是它们在 <u> 军队 </u> 中发挥作用、协助 <u> 警察 </u> 工作的原因之一。 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
